correctness.rationale: For every fixed 0<a<1, let m=min(a,1-a), r=m/16, rho=m^2/256. Expanding the cubic g_a about binary s_i gives slope -alpha_i in {a,1-a}; the map on complex l-infinity v has sup bound [rho(2+4r)+(2+r)r^2]/m<r and Lipschitz [4rho+4r+3r^2]/m<1/2. Banach contraction and analytic iteration construct the unique ball solution for |d|<rho, uniformly for all two-sided binary codes. The coefficient recurrence has dependency radius n at order n. At first reachable order R the only changed terms follow the unique left/right paths; repeated divisions by alpha_j give exact leading coefficient (s_{i-R}-t_{i-R})/prod_{j=i-R+1}^{i}alpha_j+(s_{i+R}-t_{i+R})/prod_{j=i}^{i+R-1}alpha_j. Single endpoint flips are nonzero, opposite flips cancel precisely at equal path weights; at a!=1/2 this is equal zero counts, at a=1/2 automatically. Uniform Cauchy bounds give 2r (|d|/rho)^R/(1-|d|/rho). The independent rational Taylor recursion checked 60 bounded heterogeneous/single/two-boundary instances, not the infinite proof.
